findings.evidence: template/scripts/machine_pool.py run_weight_lines raises PoolError("cannot resolve the heavy-run weight") when resolve_jobs fails. status_text calls it unconditionally while building `lines`, before the holders and waiters sections. The diagnostic command used to inspect a stuck pool therefore fails on a bad environment variable, and this is pinned by test_an_invalid_test_jobs_value_fails_explicitly. Printing the pool state first and reporting the weight problem as a line or warning would keep status usable.
findings.summary: The read-only `machine_pool.py status` now aborts entirely when DEV_PLATFORM_TEST_JOBS is invalid, or when the memory-pressure sysctl cannot be read. It prints no configuration, holders or queue in those cases.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/select_checks.py lease_weight returns 1 when every command is labelled in LIGHT_EVIDENCE_TYPES and there is no precheck. Nested run_test_groups is capped at the lease weight, so a mislabelled command would run its tests serially, while a `configuration` command that is heavy but not a test run still holds only one token. The design records this as a deliberate trade-off, but the docs don't tell project authors that labelling a command `configuration` or `syntax` lowers its pool weight.
findings.summary: A one-token lease depends only on the project's `evidence_types` labels. A command labelled `configuration` or `syntax` that actually starts a parallel test run is still limited to one token by the pool.
